text: IsEven M means B(x,x) belongs to 2ℤ for every x in M, exactly the even-lattice convention in [Dolgachev §1.1](https://sites.lsa.umich.edu/idolga-new/wp-content/uploads/sites/1467/2024/08/bourbaki83.pdf#page=3). The rational norm is B(x,x), not its half. This predicate requires neither nondegeneracy nor a separately supplied full-lattice structure on M. Published [control](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/LinearAlgebra/IntegralLattice/Overlattice/Isotropic.lean#L97) passes, [control](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/LinearAlgebra/IntegralLattice/Overlattice/Isotropic.lean#L108) passes.
Elementwise evenness is the defining predicate.
At the original carrier the predicate is precisely lattice evenness.

Writing the norms of x+y, x and y as 2a, 2b and 2c gives B(x,y)=a−b−c. Thus every pairing in M is integral, exactly the polarization implication behind [Nikulin §1.4](https://www.mathnet.ru/php/getFT.phtml?jrnid=im&option_lang=eng&paperid=1677&what=fullteng#page=8). The argument uses symmetry over ℚ and closure under addition; nondegeneracy is unnecessary. Published [control](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/LinearAlgebra/IntegralLattice/Overlattice/Isotropic.lean#L174) passes.
An even full carrier packages as an even integral lattice.

The constructor retains the actual carrier M and ambient form B. Its integrality hypothesis supplies B(M,M)⊆ℤ, and the separate IsLattice instance supplies a full finite lattice, matching [Dolgachev §1.1](https://sites.lsa.umich.edu/idolga-new/wp-content/uploads/sites/1467/2024/08/bourbaki83.pdf#page=3). For degenerate L, fullness of an arbitrary intermediate carrier is not inferred. Published [control](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/LinearAlgebra/IntegralLattice/Overlattice/Isotropic.lean#L155) passes, [control](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/LinearAlgebra/IntegralLattice/Overlattice/Isotropic.lean#L161) passes, [control](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/LinearAlgebra/IntegralLattice/Overlattice/Isotropic.lean#L167) passes.
The original intermediate carrier is retained.
The common rational form is retained.
Packaging the original carrier returns L.

An even overlattice N with N.form=L.form has B(x,x)∈2ℤ for every vector of its intermediate carrier, since that carrier is exactly N.carrier. This is the even-overlattice convention in [Nikulin §1.4](https://www.mathnet.ru/php/getFT.phtml?jrnid=im&option_lang=eng&paperid=1677&what=fullteng#page=8). Equality of forms is explicit; evenness of the smaller lattice alone would not suffice. Published [control](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/LinearAlgebra/IntegralLattice/Overlattice/Isotropic.lean#L295) passes.
The intermediate-carrier conversion recovers the original lattice.

Converting N to its intermediate carrier and packaging it again returns N by equality of its actual carrier and form. This is the literal common-ambient construction used in [Nikulin §1.4](https://www.mathnet.ru/php/getFT.phtml?jrnid=im&option_lang=eng&paperid=1677&what=fullteng#page=8). The statement retains the full-lattice instance and form equality; it claims equality, not merely an abstract isometry. Published [control](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/LinearAlgebra/IntegralLattice/Overlattice/Basic.lean#L271) passes, [control](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/LinearAlgebra/IntegralLattice/Overlattice/Isotropic.lean#L161) passes.
Conversion preserves the original carrier.
Repackaging preserves the common rational form.

IsIntegral M is the containment M⊆Mᵛ for the original form, equivalently B(x,y)∈ℤ for every x,y∈M. This is the integral-overlattice condition in [Nikulin §1.4](https://www.mathnet.ru/php/getFT.phtml?jrnid=im&option_lang=eng&paperid=1677&what=fullteng#page=8). All cross-pairings are required: integral diagonal norms alone would be weaker. The definition also permits degenerate forms. Published [control](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/LinearAlgebra/IntegralLattice/Overlattice/Isotropic.lean#L87) passes, [control](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/LinearAlgebra/IntegralLattice/Overlattice/Isotropic.lean#L102) passes.
The containment unfolds to all pairings being integral.
The original integral carrier satisfies the predicate.

Packaging an integral full intermediate carrier preserves that exact submodule of V. This agrees with the common-ambient overlattice convention in [Nikulin §1.4](https://www.mathnet.ru/php/getFT.phtml?jrnid=im&option_lang=eng&paperid=1677&what=fullteng#page=8). The equality follows from ofSubmodule’s carrier field; no basis or abstract replacement of M is chosen. Published [control](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/LinearAlgebra/IntegralLattice/Overlattice/Isotropic.lean#L167) passes.
The original carrier repackages to the original lattice.

Packaging M retains L.form literally, as required for the common-ambient overlattices of [Nikulin §1.4](https://www.mathnet.ru/php/getFT.phtml?jrnid=im&option_lang=eng&paperid=1677&what=fullteng#page=8). This is the form field of ofSubmodule, independent of the chosen integrality proof. The equality concerns the rational form, not equality of the two integral carriers. Published [control](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/LinearAlgebra/IntegralLattice/Overlattice/Isotropic.lean#L185) passes.
Positive definiteness agrees because the ambient form is identical.

This equivalence unfolds evenness to ∀x∈M, ∃n∈ℤ, B(x,x)=2n, matching [Dolgachev §1.1](https://sites.lsa.umich.edu/idolga-new/wp-content/uploads/sites/1467/2024/08/bourbaki83.pdf#page=3). The integer witness may depend on x, and the ambient norm is the full self-pairing. No positive-definiteness, nondegeneracy or finite-index condition is inserted. Published [control](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/LinearAlgebra/IntegralLattice/Overlattice/Isotropic.lean#L108) passes.
At M=L this agrees exactly with lattice evenness.

The defining inclusion M⊆Mᵛ unfolds to B(x,y)∈ℤ for every x,y∈M. Here the submodule denoted 1 is the integer span of 1 in ℚ. This is precisely the pairing condition for integral overlattices in [Nikulin §1.4](https://www.mathnet.ru/php/getFT.phtml?jrnid=im&option_lang=eng&paperid=1677&what=fullteng#page=8), including degenerate forms. Published [control](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/LinearAlgebra/IntegralLattice/Overlattice/Isotropic.lean#L102) passes.
The original integral carrier has integral pairings.

The intermediate carrier of N is N.carrier, and equality N.form=L.form transfers N’s integral pairings to L.form. This matches the common-form integral overlattices of [Nikulin §1.4](https://www.mathnet.ru/php/getFT.phtml?jrnid=im&option_lang=eng&paperid=1677&what=fullteng#page=8). The upper containment in Lᵛ follows from integrality and L⊆N; no evenness assumption is needed. Published [control](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/LinearAlgebra/IntegralLattice/Overlattice/Isotropic.lean#L295) passes.
Converting and repackaging recovers N.

The carrier field of the glued lattice is exactly the inverse image of H under Lᵛ→Lᵛ/L, the construction in [Nikulin §1.4](https://www.mathnet.ru/php/getFT.phtml?jrnid=im&option_lang=eng&paperid=1677&what=fullteng#page=8). This projection theorem preserves the specified embedded subgroup rather than choosing an abstract lattice with the same discriminant data. Published [control](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/LinearAlgebra/IntegralLattice/Overlattice/Isotropic.lean#L456) passes.
Gluing the zero subgroup returns L.

The gluing constructor leaves the rational bilinear form unchanged, as in the overlattice construction of [Nikulin §1.4](https://www.mathnet.ru/php/getFT.phtml?jrnid=im&option_lang=eng&paperid=1677&what=fullteng#page=8). This theorem is the literal form-field equality after packaging the inverse-image carrier. It does not assert that the integral carriers coincide. Published [control](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/LinearAlgebra/IntegralLattice/Overlattice/Isotropic.lean#L449) passes.
The same ambient form has the same positive-definiteness property.

Every vector in the packaged lattice is a vector of M, with the same norm. The supplied evenness of M therefore gives an even lattice, after polarization supplies integrality. This matches [Dolgachev §1.1](https://sites.lsa.umich.edu/idolga-new/wp-content/uploads/sites/1467/2024/08/bourbaki83.pdf#page=3). The separate full-lattice instance is retained; evenness is not inherited merely from L. Published [control](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/LinearAlgebra/IntegralLattice/Overlattice/Isotropic.lean#L108) passes, [control](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/LinearAlgebra/IntegralLattice/Overlattice/Isotropic.lean#L155) passes.
Evenness on the original carrier agrees with L.IsEven.
Packaging preserves the exact carrier.

The packaged overlattice has exactly L.form, so its radical remains zero when L is nondegenerate. This is the common rational-space convention of [Nikulin §1.4](https://www.mathnet.ru/php/getFT.phtml?jrnid=im&option_lang=eng&paperid=1677&what=fullteng#page=8). Nondegeneracy of L also supplies fullness of M; integrality alone would not imply nondegeneracy. Published [control](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/LinearAlgebra/IntegralLattice/Overlattice/Isotropic.lean#L161) passes.
The ambient rational form is literally unchanged.

I≤J gives V(J)⊆V(I), so the displayed reverse Lie-dimension inequality forces equality of tangent dimensions. For smooth connected subgroups, [Milne, Proposition 10.15](https://www.jmilne.org/math/Books/iAG2022.pdf#page=202) then forces equality. [The automatic inequality](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/HopfIdeal/Cotangent.lean#L423) and [kernel rigidity](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/HopfIdeal/Smooth/Containment.lean#L58) check the two steps. Both smoothness and connectedness hypotheses are retained.
Ideal inclusion reverses the quotient Lie-dimension inequality.
Both smooth connected groups and zero conormal image force the surjective coordinate kernel to vanish.

[The docstring’s](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/HopfIdeal/Smooth/Dimension.lean#L107) “members contained in the given one” reverses the subgroup direction. Its hypothesis K≤I means V(K) contains V(I), so “containing” is required. The [preceding comparison](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/HopfIdeal/Smooth/Dimension.lean#L59) and [Milne, proof of Proposition 6.42](https://www.jmilne.org/math/Books/iAG2022.pdf#page=145) confirm this. For the family {1,Gₐ}, the identity satisfies domination over contained members yet is not maximal. The Lean theorem itself is correctly oriented.
Nested smooth connected subgroups with equal Lie dimension coincide; the direction is explicit.

A nonempty family has an attained maximal Lie dimension, and smooth connected comparison makes that member maximal as a subgroup, hence minimal as an ideal. This isolates the maximality step in [Milne, proof of Proposition 6.42](https://www.jmilne.org/math/Books/iAG2022.pdf#page=145). [The bounded dimension selection](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/HopfIdeal/Cotangent.lean#L385) checks existence. No product closure, normality, uniqueness or greatest member is asserted.
The attained finite Lie dimensions of a nonempty family admit a maximum.
Nested smooth connected subgroups with equal Lie dimension coincide; the direction is explicit.

The identity section evaluates functions by the counit, so its defining ideal is precisely ker ε, as in [Milne, 10.6](https://www.jmilne.org/math/Books/iAG2022.pdf#page=199). This works already for a commutative bialgebra representing an affine monoid. [The augmentation representative formula](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/Tangent/Cotangent.lean#L107) checks its use; no antipode, smoothness or field assumption is needed.
On augmentation elements, the first-order displacement is the ordinary class modulo m².

This is m/m² for m=ker ε, the augmentation cotangent module of [Milne, 10.6](https://www.jmilne.org/math/Books/iAG2022.pdf#page=199). The name “space” specializes to a vector space over a field; the implementation correctly allows base rings and affine monoids. [The inverse-duality representative formula](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/Tangent/Cotangent.lean#L290) checks its universal first-order meaning without any smoothness hypothesis.
The inverse duality evaluates a derivation on an augmentation representative, after coefficient identification.

The map sends a to [a−ε(a)] in m/m², using the algebra map to regard ε(a) as a scalar in A. This is the displacement behind [Milne, 10.6](https://www.jmilne.org/math/Books/iAG2022.pdf#page=199). [Unit vanishing](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/Tangent/Cotangent.lean#L100) and [the counit Leibniz rule](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/Tangent/Cotangent.lean#L118) check the intended linear, first-order map.
The unit has zero first-order displacement.
The displacement obeys the Leibniz rule with counit scalar coefficients.

The displayed representative is a−algebraMap(ε(a)), whose counit is zero because ε splits the scalar map. Passing to m/m² gives exactly the displacement construction of [Milne, 10.6](https://www.jmilne.org/math/Books/iAG2022.pdf#page=199). [Its augmentation specialization](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/Tangent/Cotangent.lean#L107) checks that centering disappears when ε(a)=0, with no choice of representatives.
On augmentation elements, the first-order displacement is the ordinary class modulo m².

For x∈m the counit vanishes, so x−ε(x)=x and cotangentMap is the canonical projection m→m/m². This matches [Milne, 10.6](https://www.jmilne.org/math/Books/iAG2022.pdf#page=199). [Inverse cotangent duality](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/Tangent/Cotangent.lean#L290) checks that evaluating a derivation on such a representative recovers its functional on the quotient.
The inverse duality evaluates a derivation on an augmentation representative, after coefficient identification.

Modulo m², the product of the two displacements vanishes, leaving d(ab)=ε(a)d(b)+ε(b)d(a). This is precisely the identity-point derivation rule in [Milne, Proposition 10.28](https://www.jmilne.org/math/Books/iAG2022.pdf#page=206). [The duality evaluation formula](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/Tangent/Cotangent.lean#L280) checks that linear functionals therefore produce counit-valued derivations; no antipode or smoothness is used.
The duality evaluation after coefficient identification is the functional applied to first-order displacement.

A bialgebra map preserves the counit, hence carries m into m′ and m² into (m′)². Its induced cotangent map has the coordinate-map direction, as in [Mathlib’s cotangent map](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/RingTheory/Ideal/Cotangent.lean#L182). [The displacement formula](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/Tangent/Cotangent.lean#L152) and [duality naturality](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/Tangent/Cotangent.lean#L314) check that its dual is the geometric differential in the reverse direction.
Cotangent mapping commutes with first-order displacement under a bialgebra map.
Cotangent duality carries the coordinate cotangent map to precomposition of derivations.

Counit compatibility and preservation of scalars give φ(a−ε(a))=φ(a)−ε(φ(a)); quotienting yields the stated equation. This checks [Mathlib’s cotangent map](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/RingTheory/Ideal/Cotangent.lean#L182) on the generators of the cotangent module. [The duality naturality theorem](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/Tangent/Cotangent.lean#L314) confirms the corresponding precomposition formula for derivations, without finiteness assumptions.
Cotangent duality carries the coordinate cotangent map to precomposition of derivations.

A counit-valued derivation kills m² and scalars, so restriction to m descends uniquely; conversely f defines a↦f([a−ε(a)]). This is [Milne, Proposition 10.28](https://www.jmilne.org/math/Books/iAG2022.pdf#page=206), generalized to rings. [The inverse formula](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/Tangent/Cotangent.lean#L290) checks the factorization. B may be noncommutative: the A-action factors through central scalar values, making the equivalence B-linear.
The inverse duality evaluates a derivation on an augmentation representative, after coefficient identification.
The duality evaluation after coefficient identification is the functional applied to first-order displacement.

The constructed derivation evaluates f on the centered cotangent class of a, exactly the forward map in [Milne, Proposition 10.28](https://www.jmilne.org/math/Books/iAG2022.pdf#page=206). The right side is read in the counit coefficient synonym. [The explicit coefficient-identification formula](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/Tangent/Cotangent.lean#L280) checks that transport and preserves the stated generality to noncommutative coefficient rings.
The duality evaluation after coefficient identification is the functional applied to first-order displacement.

After the canonical identification of CounitAlgebra with B, the derived tangent vector has value f([a−ε(a)]), as in [Milne, Proposition 10.28](https://www.jmilne.org/math/Books/iAG2022.pdf#page=206). This makes the coefficient transport explicit. [The inverse evaluation](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/Tangent/Cotangent.lean#L290) checks recovery on augmentation representatives; it does not require B to be commutative or cotangents finite.
The inverse duality evaluates a derivation on an augmentation representative, after coefficient identification.

The inverse equivalence sends [x], x∈m, to d(x) under the coefficient identification. This is well-defined because the counit Leibniz rule makes d vanish on m², as in [Milne, Proposition 10.28](https://www.jmilne.org/math/Books/iAG2022.pdf#page=206). [The augmentation formula](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/Tangent/Cotangent.lean#L107) checks the inverse relationship; representatives need not be unique.
On augmentation elements, the first-order displacement is the ordinary class modulo m².

Both sides evaluate a as f([φ(a)−ε(φ(a))]); counit compatibility identifies the two coefficient actions. Thus the cotangent dual map is precomposition of derivations, as in [Milne, Proposition 10.28](https://www.jmilne.org/math/Books/iAG2022.pdf#page=206). [The coefficient-R specialization](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/Tangent/Cotangent.lean#L326) and [composition law](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/Tangent/Cotangent.lean#L360) check the contravariant differential convention.
At coefficients R, the dual cotangent map is exactly the differential on derivations.
Differentials compose in reverse coordinate-map order.

For finite projective M=m/m², [Mathlib’s finite-projective tensor–Hom comparison](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/LinearAlgebra/Contraction.lean#L254) gives B⊗M*≃Hom_R(M,B); cotangent duality gives the claimed B-linear equivalence. No flatness of B is required, and B may be noncommutative. [The GL matrix specialization](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/GeneralLinear/Tangent.lean#L431) and [differential compatibility](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/Tangent/Cotangent.lean#L498) check the comparison.
For GL, scalar extension on a pure tangent tensor is coefficientwise matrix extension followed by scalar multiplication.
Finite-projective tangent scalar extension intertwines the cotangent differential with precomposition of coefficient-valued derivations.

The pure tensor b⊗f evaluates as b·algebraMap(f([a−ε(a)])), the evaluation map in [Mathlib’s finite-projective tensor–Hom comparison](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/LinearAlgebra/Contraction.lean#L254). The scalar lies centrally in B, so this multiplication order remains valid for noncommutative B. [The coefficient-identification formula](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/Tangent/Cotangent.lean#L470) checks the value in the original ring; finite projectivity remains explicit.
The pure tensor comparison has the claimed value in the underlying coefficient ring, including noncommutative coefficients.

Erasing the counit coefficient synonym yields b·algebraMap(f([a−ε(a)])), exactly [Mathlib’s finite-projective tensor–Hom comparison](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/LinearAlgebra/Contraction.lean#L254) followed by cotangent duality. The scalar factor is central even when B is noncommutative. [The GL coefficient-extension formula](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/GeneralLinear/Tangent.lean#L405) checks the classical specialization; this is an evaluation identity, not a new smoothness assertion.
For GL, the tensor 1⊗f maps the tangent matrix entries through the scalar map.

The tensor b⊗f becomes the R-valued tangent vector of f, postcomposed with R→B and multiplied by b. This is the bundled form of [Mathlib’s finite-projective tensor–Hom comparison](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/LinearAlgebra/Contraction.lean#L254). [The SL root-vector specialization](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/SpecialLinear/Root/Adjoint.lean#L133) checks the intended coefficient normalization, while the general statement retains finite projectivity and allows noncommutative B.
For SL root vectors, scalar extension agrees with the actual additive root-subgroup differential at the same coefficient.

The identity interval map is bundled as the path from zero to one in I. Its value at time t is t, with continuity and both endpoints inherited directly from the identity continuous map. This is an actual path in the interval, rather than a constant path serving as an identity in the fundamental groupoid. Compared with [§1.1 pp25–27: interval paths, concatenation and reversal](https://pi.math.cornell.edu/~hatcher/AT/ATch1.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Topology/Path.lean#L136).

Casting changes the endpoint labels using the equalities x′=x and y′=y, while preserving every value γ(t). Consequently the same continuity proof applies and only the endpoint equalities need transport. This is the type-level version of regarding one path with equal descriptions of its endpoints; it neither changes time nor chooses connecting paths. Compared with [§1.1 pp25–27: interval paths, concatenation and reversal](https://pi.math.cornell.edu/~hatcher/AT/ATch1.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Topology/Path.lean#L379).

Mapping first by f and then by g equals mapping by g∘f as a bundled path, since both evaluate to g(f(γ(t))). The endpoint types agree as g(f(x)),g(f(y)), and the displayed continuity proof is hg.comp hf. This is the pre-quotient functoriality underlying the standard induced map on path classes. Compared with [§1.1 p34: postcomposition of paths and homotopies, and functoriality](https://pi.math.cornell.edu/~hatcher/AT/ATch1.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Topology/Path.lean#L372).

Postcomposing γ with the identity continuous map yields exactly γ. Path extensionality identifies the bundles once their values agree, so the continuity proof does not introduce extra data into the result. This is the identity law for the same postcomposition operation used to induce maps on path classes. Compared with [§1.1 p34: postcomposition of paths and homotopies, and functoriality](https://pi.math.cornell.edu/~hatcher/AT/ATch1.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Topology/Path.lean#L367).

The concatenated path evaluates γ at 2t when t≤1/2 and γ′ at 2t−1 otherwise, matching first-γ-then-γ′ traversal. The dependent branches include proofs that these rescaled times lie in I. At the midpoint the selected first branch and the second branch would both give the shared endpoint y. Compared with [§1.1 pp25–27: interval paths, concatenation and reversal](https://pi.math.cornell.edu/~hatcher/AT/ATch1.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Topology/Path.lean#L288).

The image of a concatenated path is exactly the union of its two constituent images. The rescaled first and second half-intervals cover every original time in their respective paths, so this is equality rather than mere containment. The typed common endpoint supplies a valid concatenation without any injectivity or disjointness requirement. Compared with [§1.1 pp25–27: interval paths, concatenation and reversal](https://pi.math.cornell.edu/~hatcher/AT/ATch1.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Topology/Path.lean#L328).

Reversing a path preserves its image because t↦1−t permutes the entire closed interval. The proof uses surjectivity of this interval involution, giving both inclusions even if γ is noninjective. Thus orientation changes while the traversed subset does not, as required by the standard reversal convention. Compared with [§1.1 pp25–27: interval paths, concatenation and reversal](https://pi.math.cornell.edu/~hatcher/AT/ATch1.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Topology/Path.lean#L169).

Reversing twice returns the identical bundled path: the time coordinate becomes 1−(1−t)=t and the endpoint order is restored. The equality is pointwise before taking homotopy classes. It does not assert that concatenation of a path with its reversal is pointwise constant, which would fail for a nonconstant path. Compared with [§1.1 pp25–27: interval paths, concatenation and reversal](https://pi.math.cornell.edu/~hatcher/AT/ATch1.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Topology/Path.lean#L160).

Extending γ constantly outside I does not change its image. The original interval values all remain, and the added tails contribute only the source and target, which γ already attains. This is the range property of the explicit interval projection used by extend, not a statement about arbitrary continuous extensions. Compared with [§1.1 pp25–27: interval paths, concatenation and reversal](https://pi.math.cornell.edu/~hatcher/AT/ATch1.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Topology/Path.lean#L229).

Reversal commutes with constant extension after changing real time by t↦1−t. Interval projection respects this reflection, so the formula holds on all ℝ. In particular the left tail of the reversed path corresponds to the right tail of the original one, and vice versa, with the swapped endpoint values. Compared with [§1.1 pp25–27: interval paths, concatenation and reversal](https://pi.math.cornell.edu/~hatcher/AT/ATch1.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Topology/Path.lean#L250).

For every real t≥1/2, the extension of γ₁ followed by γ₂ evaluates as γ₂.extend(2t−1). The formula includes the midpoint, where both paths meet, and times beyond one, where both sides are the final endpoint. It is the second branch of concatenation extended consistently to the full real half-line. Compared with [§1.1 pp25–27: interval paths, concatenation and reversal](https://pi.math.cornell.edu/~hatcher/AT/ATch1.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Topology/Path.lean#L315).

For every real t≤1/2, the extended concatenation evaluates as γ₁.extend(2t). The proof separates nonpositive times, where both sides equal the source, from interval times, where the first concatenation branch applies. The inclusive midpoint gives the shared endpoint, agreeing with the second branch as well. Compared with [§1.1 pp25–27: interval paths, concatenation and reversal](https://pi.math.cornell.edu/~hatcher/AT/ATch1.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Topology/Path.lean#L309).

The image of the constant path at a is exactly {a}. Containment follows from its constant value, while equality uses the nonempty unit interval to attain a. This elementary range identity agrees with the constant path convention and does not confuse the constant path with the empty image of a function on an empty domain. Compared with [§1.1 pp25–27: interval paths, concatenation and reversal](https://pi.math.cornell.edu/~hatcher/AT/ATch1.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Topology/Path.lean#L149).

The affine homotopy sends (t,x) along the straight segment from f(x) to g(x), equivalently (1−t)•f(x)+t•g(x). Hatcher’s linear construction extends from Euclidean paths to arbitrary continuous maps into the stated real topological module: continuous addition and scalar multiplication give joint continuity, and t=0,1 give f,g. No norm or finite dimension is used. Compared with [Example1.1 p25: linear homotopy and continuity from vector operations](https://pi.math.cornell.edu/~hatcher/AT/ATch1.pdf); [Chapter0 p3: homotopy of arbitrary continuous maps](https://pi.math.cornell.edu/~hatcher/AT/ATch0.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Topology/Homotopy/Affine.lean#L31).

The reflexive relative homotopy is F(t,x)=f(x), constant in the homotopy parameter. Hence it fixes every point of S at its f-value, exactly as required by homotopy relative to a subset. The construction works for any S without an openness, closedness or nonemptiness assumption. Compared with [Chapter0 p3: homotopy relative to a subspace](https://pi.math.cornell.edu/~hatcher/AT/ATch0.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Topology/Homotopy/Basic.lean#L568).

Postcomposition of an endpoint-fixed path homotopy F with a continuous map f gives the endpoint-fixed homotopy f∘F between the mapped paths. The source separately checks the two homotopy-time boundaries and both path endpoints. This is the construction that makes induced maps on path homotopy classes well-defined, including distinct endpoints. Compared with [§1.1 p34: postcomposition of paths and homotopies, and functoriality](https://pi.math.cornell.edu/~hatcher/AT/ATch1.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Topology/Homotopy/Path.lean#L226).

Equal endpoint labels allow the same square F to serve as a homotopy between the cast paths. Path.cast changes no interval values, and path homotopy is defined relative to the interval endpoints {0,1}; consequently all boundary data and continuity remain unchanged. The definition returns the original homotopy rather than selecting a replacement. Compared with [§1.1 pp25–26: endpoint-fixed homotopy and its equivalence classes](https://pi.math.cornell.edu/~hatcher/AT/ATch1.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Topology/Homotopy/Path.lean#L143).

Existence of a fixed-endpoint homotopy is unchanged when both paths are relabeled by the same endpoint equalities. The source can reuse the existing nonempty homotopy type directly because endpoint casting preserves the underlying continuous maps. Thus the proposition retains the original relative-endpoint relation without any appeal to free homotopy. Compared with [§1.1 pp25–26: endpoint-fixed homotopy and its equivalence classes](https://pi.math.cornell.edu/~hatcher/AT/ATch1.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Topology/Homotopy/Path.lean#L280).

Mapping a path class by g∘f equals first mapping it by f and then by g. On a representative both sides are the same postcomposed interval function; respect for endpoint-fixed homotopy makes this independent of the representative. This is Hatcher’s induced-map composition law generalized from loops to paths with two possibly different endpoints. Compared with [§1.1 p34: postcomposition of paths and homotopies, and functoriality](https://pi.math.cornell.edu/~hatcher/AT/ATch1.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Topology/Homotopy/Path.lean#L406).

Equality of two classes in the quotient by endpoint-fixed path homotopy implies that the represented paths are homotopic in that same sense. The quotient uses the proved equivalence relation Homotopic, so equality does not merely certify a chain of weaker relations. The conclusion is existence of a continuous homotopy fixing both endpoints, not equality of the original paths. Compared with [§1.1 pp25–26: endpoint-fixed homotopy and its equivalence classes](https://pi.math.cornell.edu/~hatcher/AT/ATch1.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Topology/Homotopy/Path.lean#L315).

A positive element is strictly larger than its half. The alias selects the correct implication of half_lt_self_iff. The actual assumptions give an ordered semifield with positive, nonzero 2, so no division-by-zero case is hidden. Compared with [the reference](https://jirilebl.github.io/ra/html/sec_basicpropsrn.html) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Algebra/Order/Field/Basic.lean#L128).

Half of a positive element is positive. The proof divides two positive elements, using positivity of 2 from the strict ordered-semiring structure. The statement applies to semifields and needs no additive inverses. Compared with [the reference](https://jirilebl.github.io/ra/html/sec_basicpropsrn.html) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Algebra/Order/Field/Basic.lean#L112).

Inversion preserves nonnegativity under the stated group-with-zero order assumptions. The zero case is included because 0⁻¹=0. The proof separates equality with zero from strict positivity and uses the inverse-sign equivalence. Compared with [the reference](https://jirilebl.github.io/ra/html/sec_basicpropsrn.html) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Algebra/Order/GroupWithZero/Basic.lean#L845).

An element has positive inverse exactly when it is positive. The proof uses strict-order reflection by nonnegative left factors and then double inversion for the reverse implication. Addition, commutativity and total order are unnecessary. Compared with [the reference](https://jirilebl.github.io/ra/html/sec_basicpropsrn.html) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Algebra/Order/GroupWithZero/Basic.lean#L836).

The product of two nonnegative elements is nonnegative when multiplication by a nonnegative left factor is monotone and zero is absorbing. The proof compares a*0 with a*b. It does not require a ring or even associativity. Compared with [the reference](https://jirilebl.github.io/ra/html/sec_basicpropsrn.html) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Algebra/Order/GroupWithZero/Basic.lean#L66).

Every natural power of a positive element is positive under strict monotonicity of multiplication by positive left factors. The zero exponent is included and handled as a⁰=1; the positive input ensures nontriviality needed for 0<1. Compared with [the reference](https://jirilebl.github.io/ra/html/sec_basicpropsrn.html) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Algebra/Order/GroupWithZero/Basic.lean#L584).

For a nonzero left factor a with the stated cancellation property, a*b=a exactly when b=1. The proof compares a*b with a*1. The nonzero hypothesis is essential and is explicitly present. Compared with [the reference](https://jirilebl.github.io/ra/html/sec_basicpropsrn.html) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Algebra/GroupWithZero/Basic.lean#L295).

A nonzero element of a group with zero also satisfies the left inverse equation a⁻¹*a=1. This is derived from the supplied group-with-zero laws, so it remains valid without commutativity. Compared with [the reference](https://jirilebl.github.io/ra/html/sec_basicpropsrn.html) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Algebra/GroupWithZero/NeZero.lean#L52).

If a≤b and c≤d, then a*c≤b*d provided c and b are nonnegative and multiplication is monotone on both stated sides. The sign assumptions match the proof chain a*c≤b*c≤b*d. It does not require a to be nonnegative. Compared with [the reference](https://jirilebl.github.io/ra/html/sec_basicpropsrn.html) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Algebra/Order/GroupWithZero/Defs.lean#L351).

Left multiplication by a nonnegative element preserves a non-strict inequality under PosMulMono. The theorem exposes exactly that class law and keeps the multiplier on the left. Compared with [the reference](https://jirilebl.github.io/ra/html/sec_basicpropsrn.html) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Algebra/Order/GroupWithZero/Defs.lean#L225).

Right multiplication by a nonnegative element preserves a non-strict inequality under MulPosMono. The factor order and right-sided class assumption match the formula b*a≤c*a. Compared with [the reference](https://jirilebl.github.io/ra/html/sec_basicpropsrn.html) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Algebra/Order/GroupWithZero/Defs.lean#L229).

The distinguished one is positive when 0≤1 and 1≠0 in a partial order. This alias of zero_lt_one uses exactly the nonzeroness needed to turn the weak inequality into a strict one. Compared with [the reference](https://jirilebl.github.io/ra/html/sec_basicpropsrn.html) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Algebra/Order/ZeroLEOne.lean#L61).

The theorem exposes the supplied ZeroLEOneClass fact 0≤1, with the type parameter implicit. It assumes only the two distinguished elements, a relation ≤ and this class law. Compared with [the reference](https://jirilebl.github.io/ra/html/sec_basicpropsrn.html) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Algebra/Order/ZeroLEOne.lean#L26).

IsOrderedRing packages a semiring with a partial order, monotone addition, 0≤1 and monotonicity of multiplication by nonnegative elements on both sides. Despite its name it requires no additive inverses. These laws agree with the standard ordered-ring specialization. Compared with [the reference](https://jirilebl.github.io/ra/html/sec_basicpropsrn.html) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Algebra/Order/Ring/Defs.lean#L64).

IsStrictOrderedRing packages a nontrivial partially ordered semiring with order-preserving and order-reflecting additive translations, 0≤1, and strict monotonicity of multiplication by positive elements on both sides. The standard ordered-ring specialization agrees with these laws. Compared with [the reference](https://jirilebl.github.io/ra/html/sec_basicpropsrn.html) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Algebra/Order/Ring/Defs.lean#L74).

LinearOrderedCommGroupWithZero models a totally ordered abelian group with an absorbing least zero adjoined. Its nonzero elements form the ordered group; zero is not invertible and its total inverse is zero. This matches the multiplicative valuation convention. Compared with [the reference](https://web.math.princeton.edu/~smorel/adic_notes.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Algebra/Order/GroupWithZero/Canonical.lean#L45).

LinearOrderedCommMonoidWithZero is a commutative monoid with absorbing least zero and a linear order, with multiplication by positive elements strictly monotone. It generalizes the zero-adjoined ordered-group convention without requiring inverses. Compared with [the reference](https://web.math.princeton.edu/~smorel/adic_notes.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Algebra/Order/GroupWithZero/Canonical.lean#L41).

MulPosMono is exactly non-strict monotonicity of right multiplication by each nonnegative element. The own doc and field agree on both the multiplier side and the inclusion of zero. Compared with [the reference](https://jirilebl.github.io/ra/html/sec_basicpropsrn.html) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Algebra/Order/GroupWithZero/Defs.lean#L130).

PosMulMono is exactly non-strict monotonicity of left multiplication by each nonnegative element. Its documentation uses nonnegative, correctly including zero despite the abbreviated class name. Compared with [the reference](https://jirilebl.github.io/ra/html/sec_basicpropsrn.html) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Algebra/Order/GroupWithZero/Defs.lean#L98).

ZeroLEOneClass states precisely that the distinguished zero is related by ≤ to the distinguished one. Its own documentation and single field agree. It supplies no additional order or algebraic structure. Compared with [the reference](https://jirilebl.github.io/ra/html/sec_basicpropsrn.html) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Algebra/Order/ZeroLEOne.lean#L21).
